assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore's collateral-constraint mechanism explains how small shocks are amplified and propagated through asset prices and credit limits. It became a core building block of macro-finance and of quantitative macroeconomic models, and it shaped the post-2008 analysis of crises. The idea is foundational, tractable and widely reused.
assessment.attribution: The central 1997 credit-cycles contribution is clearly Kiyotaki and Moore's. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator and empirical strand, which Bernanke and Gertler developed and which is partly recognised already. Restricting the credit to the two originators of the collateral-constraint dynamics is clean.
assessment.maturity: About three decades of confirmation, with extensive theoretical extension and empirical application to housing, firm investment and crises. The timing is ample.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit the financial-accelerator strand (Gertler, Gilchrist) alongside it.
Overlap with the earlier 2022 banking and financial-crisis recognition could reduce the novelty weight.
Direct empirical identification of collateral channels is more mixed than the theory's influence suggests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work links optimal tax theory to behavioural elasticities and sufficient-statistics methods. It changed how the revenue and efficiency costs of taxation are measured, and it feeds directly into policy design on top rates and tax avoidance. The contribution is substantial and has real-world effect.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are the strongest pair for the taxable-income elasticity and tax-avoidance-response literature. Chetty's sufficient-statistics work and Stantcheva's dynamic and behavioural optimal-tax work are important but are better credited elsewhere or are more recent. Feldstein, who originated the elasticity concept, is not on the list and, as far as I know, has died.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of evidence from many countries and tax reforms. The framework is established, although the estimated elasticities remain debated.
uncertainties: Saez also appears on another ballot, so a combined credit might be preferred.
Estimates of the elasticity of taxable income are sensitive to method and context.
Feldstein's prior role in the idea complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sticky-price modelling and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary-policy analysis and central-bank practice. The Taylor rule gave a transparent description of policy, Woodford provided the rigorous microfounded synthesis, and Calvo's time-dependent pricing is the workhorse. The discovery is of first-order importance for macroeconomics and policy.
assessment.attribution: The field has many contributors (Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others). Three names cover the pricing mechanism, the policy rule and the theoretical synthesis, but any cut is somewhat arbitrary and leaves strong contributors out. Prior prizes in this area (Phelps, Lucas, Kydland-Prescott, Sargent-Sims) narrow the unclaimed space.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of use in central banks and DSGE models, although the framework was strongly challenged after 2008 and again by post-pandemic inflation.
uncertainties: Attribution breadth and the three-laureate limit.
Whether post-pandemic inflation weakens the case for the baseline framework.
Overlap with earlier macroeconomics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini built the modern theory and empirics of how political institutions (electoral rules, constitutions, forms of government) shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. They brought political economy fully into mainstream economics, and the field is now large and influential.
assessment.attribution: The core of the research programme and the widely used synthesis book are principally theirs. Besley's contributions on state capacity and accountability are also major, so excluding him is a difficult judgement. Acemoglu, Robinson and Johnson received the 2024 prize on institutions, which partly overlaps in subject if not in approach.
assessment.maturity: Developed over about 30 years with large empirical follow-up. Some causal-identification questions about institutional effects remain.
uncertainties: Possible proximity to the 2024 institutions prize.
Whether Besley should be included given the three-name limit.
Institutional or collegial connections to members of the Stockholm environment are disclosed but not adjudicated here, and I have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large-scale administrative data gave the first credible, granular measurement of intergenerational mobility and of neighbourhood and place effects on children's outcomes. It changed both research design and the policy debate on opportunity. Chetty's wider body of work also has substantial methodological influence.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear lead. Hendren is central to the neighbourhood-effects and exposure-effects work. Friedman and Katz are significant collaborators, but credit would be more diffuse with them included. Sibling work, such as the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis, is collaborative.
assessment.maturity: The main results date from about 2014 onward, so the work is mature in impact but relatively recent. Replication and the interpretation of causal place effects are still developing.
uncertainties: Recency compared with other candidates.
Debate over whether the evidence is causal or descriptive.
Attribution within a large collaborative team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity trade model changed the unit of analysis from industries to firms. It explains selection, exporter premia and a new channel for gains from trade, and it reshaped empirical trade research and policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the single central paper. Helpman supplied the broader firm-level research programme, with Melitz and Yeaple on exports versus FDI and the Helpman-Melitz-Rubinstein gravity work. Redding is a major follower, but his work is less foundational. Krugman has already received the prize for new trade theory.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of extensive empirical validation and extensions. The framework is standard in trade courses and policy models.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier new-trade-theory prize.
Helpman also appears on another trade ballot, so credit may be split.
Quantitative-trade and gains-from-trade literatures overlap with this one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantifying how misallocation of inputs across firms lowers aggregate productivity gave a disciplined account of cross-country income differences. It became a standard tool in growth and development economics and relates to the broader question of why countries differ in prosperity.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 Hsieh-Klenow paper is the centre of the contribution. Restuccia and Rogerson's closely related work developed the idea in parallel, and Restuccia is credited on this ballot. Rogerson is not on it, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited and widely applied since 2009, but the measurement approach has been challenged on how misallocation is inferred from data, including measurement error and model sensitivity.
uncertainties: Parallel work by Restuccia and Rogerson complicates credit.
Sensitivity of misallocation estimates to measurement and model assumptions.
Relatively short track record for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour-market polarisation, trade exposure and the distribution of adjustment costs. The work is empirically influential and policy-relevant, with a strong link to the automation and AI debates.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both strands, task-based change and trade shocks. Hanson shares the trade-shock work. Dorn and Katz are strong coauthors, and Katz also appears on another ballot. Acemoglu's role in the task-based framework is outside this ballot and was partly recognised in the 2024 prize.
assessment.maturity: The main empirical work is from the 2000s and 2010s. Its long-run interpretation and the persistence of local effects are still debated and revised.
uncertainties: Overlap with themes of the 2024 prize.
Debate over the size and persistence of the China shock.
Credit division among several close collaborators.
